title: AutoHealOps
subtitle: Infrastructure intelligence & guarded recovery
description: An operations console for workload telemetry, explainable fault detection, and bounded recovery workflows, with an isolated public browser simulation.
users: Operators learning to inspect faults and review constrained recovery actions.
features: Cluster explorer, incident and audit views
Local anomaly pipeline and guarded recovery controller
challenges: The public demo has no cluster or trained model attached. Real-cluster acceptance remains pending; the local controller is not an HA production control plane.

architectureReference:
flowchart LR
  UI[React console] -->|REST + WS| API[FastAPI control plane]

problem: Operators need to connect abnormal workload behavior to bounded, reviewable recovery actions.
solution: Provide telemetry, evidence, incidents, and guarded healing controls while separating public simulation from optional real adapters.
technicalDetails: The public browser adapter keeps visitor simulations local. The optional backend supplies persistent events, telemetry, and an anomaly service.
Recovery code enforces namespace and ownership boundaries, budgets, cooldowns, and pause states. Real Kubernetes interaction is optional and has its own validation requirements.

title: FlowNovaAI
subtitle: Agent workflow automation concept
description: A newly created repository describing an AI agent workflow automation builder.
users: Intended direction: a builder for agent automation workflows.
features: Repository initialized with a project description
challenges: Only a two-line README is present in the inspected commit. No application, architecture, technology choices, or implemented features are claimed.
problem: The README identifies agent workflow automation as the intended problem area.
solution: A workflow builder is the stated direction; no implementation or concrete solution architecture has been published.
technicalDetails: The inspected repository contains README.md only. No dependency manifest, application source, or screenshot assets were present.

title: DSA Preparation
subtitle: Patterns, practice, and recall
description: A structured collection of algorithm solutions, pattern notes, contest work, and synchronized LeetCode progress.
users: Interview preparation and deliberate algorithm practice.
challenges: README sections contain snapshots from different dates. The portfolio reads current counts independently from the official LeetCode endpoint rather than treating historical badges as live.

problem: Repeated practice is less useful when solutions and patterns are scattered or difficult to revisit.
solution: Organize implementations by topic and maintain public progress snapshots through synchronization workflows.
technicalDetails: Topic folders organize implementations and learning notes by recurring problem patterns, with separate contest practice.
The repository contains dated statistics blocks. Historical solved totals and the current portfolio API are intentionally treated as different verification moments.

title: TraceHunt AI
subtitle: Evidence-based incident investigation
description: An observability workspace bringing endpoint checks, structured logs, anomaly rules, and incident evidence into one place.
users: Developers investigating service failures and correlating incident evidence.
features: HTTP monitor lifecycle and check history
Structured log ingestion and incident timelines
Local heuristic analysis with optional OpenAI enrichment
challenges: Local heuristic analysis is available without an API key. SSO, multi-tenancy, distributed tracing, and automatic remediation are outside this release.

    Web -->|same-origin API proxy| API[FastAPI]

problem: Endpoint failures, logs, and releases are difficult to reason about when evidence lives in separate tools.
solution: Bring monitors, incident timelines, and reviewable hypotheses into a single-workspace console.
technicalDetails: Monitor configuration, structured events, and incident transitions are persisted through the FastAPI/SQL layer rather than represented only as dashboard state.
A SQL outbox and background worker separate event handling from HTTP requests. Local heuristic investigations remain available when optional model integration is absent.

title: FinovaIQ
subtitle: Personal-finance workspace
description: A finance dashboard with manual accounts, precise transaction accounting, budgets, portfolios, and an explicitly labeled demo copilot.
users: People exploring manual personal-finance tracking using fictional demonstration records.
features: Persisted dashboard and optional AI adapter
architecture: Prisma / PostgreSQL; optional FastAPI AI service
challenges: No bank connections or live market prices are supplied. Browser chart approximations are separate from persisted precise monetary calculations. Redis workers remain pending.

screenshots.caption: FinovaIQ — dashboard (repository capture; demo data where shown)
FinovaIQ — mobile dashboard (repository capture; demo data where shown)

problem: Manual income, expenses, budgets, and investments need consistent accounting across views.
solution: Use a persistent API and precise monetary calculations behind a responsive finance workspace.
technicalDetails: The finance layer converts monetary strings into minor-unit BigInt values; Prisma Decimal is configured for higher-precision calculations.
The web workspace calls a NestJS API backed by Prisma/PostgreSQL. The deterministic demo copilot and optional FastAPI/OpenAI adapter have explicitly different behavior.

title: FlowPilot
subtitle: Interactive SaaS product experience
description: A responsive SaaS demonstration with a workflow sandbox, seat-based pricing calculator, and a trial configuration modal.
users: Teams evaluating an illustrative workflow product and developers studying interactive product UI.
features: Monthly/annual pricing with a seat slider
challenges: FlowPilot is a fictional brand. Workflow runs, analytics, and form submissions remain local demonstrations, rather than a connected SaaS backend.
problem: A product landing page needs to explain pricing and interaction before a visitor commits.
solution: Offer a local workflow sandbox and a calculator that preserves plan, billing cycle, and seat selections.
technicalDetails: Pricing calculations are separated from presentation components and compute monthly/annual totals, effective seats, and annual savings.
InteractiveDemo, PricingSection, and SignupModal coordinate through browser state. The repository documents that no connected SaaS backend or real signup service is included.

title: ChainPass
subtitle: One pass. More possibilities.
description: A ticketing application with transactional inventory, private wallets, signed QR admission, and optional on-chain issuance proofs.
users: Customers and organizers exploring events, transport, bookings, and admission.
features: Signed QR credentials and organizer check-in
Optional Firebase, Razorpay and durable blockchain outbox
challenges: Railway reservations and test identity checks are simulations. Real auth/payments require provider configuration. No throughput or availability SLA is claimed.

architectureReference:
flowchart LR
  B[React browser] -->|same origin /api| A[Fastify API replicas]
  A -->|transaction| P[(PostgreSQL)]

  W[Anchoring worker] --> O

  A --> S[Static frontend assets]
  B --> F[Firebase Authentication]
  B --> R[Razorpay hosted checkout]

problem: Ticketing must handle limited inventory, repeated checkout requests, and one-time admission without leaking private credentials.
solution: Use transactional booking, idempotency, signed QR admission, and optional asynchronous blockchain anchoring.
technicalDetails: Bookings and outbox writes share database transactions; conditional updates and idempotency prevent duplicate issuance and inventory overselling.
The worker leases outbox rows, renews ownership, and confirms anchoring through an adapter. SQLite supports local use while PostgreSQL provides the intended multi-replica database path.

title: LeetCode AI Sync
subtitle: From accepted submission to repository
description: A Chrome extension for detecting accepted LeetCode submissions, generating optional language variants, and pushing code through a retryable GitHub workflow.
users: Developers maintaining a searchable archive of their algorithm practice.
features: Network, DOM and polling submission detection
Provider adapters and a retry queue
challenges: Generated solutions need review. Extension permissions, provider credentials, and GitHub access require deliberate configuration; no store publication is claimed.
problem: Manually filing accepted submissions can interrupt practice and leave repository history incomplete.
solution: Detect submissions through multiple signals, queue work durably, and push reviewed outputs through GitHub adapters.
technicalDetails: The background queue uses IndexedDB, with queue records mirrored into extension storage for the interface.
Content scripts and the background worker separate browser detection from asynchronous provider and GitHub operations. Failed work can remain visible for retry.

title: Enterprise RAG Knowledge Assistant
subtitle: Searchable organizational knowledge
description: A document workspace with browser-native chunking and BM25 retrieval, plus a separately configurable FastAPI service architecture.
users: Teams exploring document retrieval and source-linked answers.
challenges: The default browser mode performs lexical retrieval and formatted answers. Selecting a model in settings does not establish a live LLM connection or enterprise SSO enforcement.
problem: A collection of documents is not useful if readers cannot find the passages relevant to a question.
solution: Chunk text, retrieve relevant excerpts, and provide cited answers in a browser-native workspace, with optional backend services.
technicalDetails: The frontend AppStore models documents, chunks, conversations, query logs, users, and retrieval settings, persisting browser state locally.
The default retrieval engine uses BM25 over text chunks. FastAPI services provide a separate optional path for binary parsing, embeddings, and other server integrations.

title: RemoteShield X
subtitle: Secure remote-work browser
description: A desktop browser and administration toolkit with Tauri, a Node gateway, VPN checks, and mobile project assets.
users: Teams investigating controlled remote browsing and central network egress.
challenges: OS-level enforcement and VPN policy need deployment-specific validation. Source presence does not establish a security certification or support guarantee.
problem: Remote browsing policies depend on device, gateway, and network behavior working together.
solution: Combine a Tauri browser, VPN checks, and a central gateway for experiments with controlled browsing.
technicalDetails: The desktop source separates browser tabs, navigation, login, and VPN guards. The Node gateway separates authentication, admin, and proxy routes.
Networking and operating-system restrictions are deployment concerns in addition to application code. Their effectiveness must be tested on each supported platform.

title: Intramind.AI
subtitle: Knowledge retrieval exploration
description: An early knowledge-platform scaffold exploring a Next.js interface and a FastAPI document-questioning architecture.
users: Teams exploring how to make internal knowledge searchable.
challenges: The checked-in RAG pipeline returns a placeholder. Production RAG, citations, and access controls described in the README are not established by the inspected implementation.
problem: Internal knowledge is spread across documents rather than a single searchable interface.
solution: Explore a document-to-answer architecture; the published implementation currently stops at scaffolds and a placeholder pipeline.
technicalDetails: The FastAPI entry point registers an API router, while a separate chat scaffold exposes a basic service response.
RAGPipeline.run currently returns a fixed placeholder response. The richer retrieval and security descriptions in the README remain unverified implementation goals.

title: MetaRole.AI
subtitle: AI career co-pilot
description: Resume analysis, skill graphs, career suggestions, and tailored document generation in a terminal-inspired workspace.
users: Job seekers comparing their skills with target roles.
challenges: Session storage is process-local; durable analysis history requires a persistent store. OpenAI features require server configuration.
problem: A resume lists skills, but does not directly explain how they fit a target role.
solution: Turn uploaded resume text into a skill graph and route the resulting context through analysis and generation endpoints.
technicalDetails: The upload flow parses PDF content before requesting analysis. The skill-analysis route returns graph nodes and edges for the interface.
Generation and prediction are separate routes sharing session context. Process-local session state makes persistence and deployment lifetime explicit trade-offs.

title: SecureRxChain
subtitle: Pharmaceutical traceability
description: A drug-batch tracking prototype combining role-based dashboards, QR verification, and wallet-signed registry interactions.
users: Manufacturers, distributors, pharmacies, and consumers exploring batch provenance.
features: Drug registry contract and QR scanner
challenges: The frontend uses Ethers.js rather than the older Web3.js portfolio label. Real contract writes require a correctly configured network and deployment.
problem: Drug batches move between several actors, making provenance and ownership difficult to inspect in one place.
solution: Separate role-specific batch workflows from wallet-signed registry interactions and metadata storage.
technicalDetails: Web3Context constructs an Ethers BrowserProvider, obtains a signer, and connects it to the DrugRegistry ABI.
The application separates user/metadata routes from the Solidity registry. A local/default contract address must be replaced for another deployment.

title: SolGuard AI
subtitle: Smart-contract audit research
description: A staged auditing prototype coordinating Solidity parsing, static checks, risk scoring, optional language-model reasoning, and patch suggestions.
users: Smart-contract developers reviewing candidate vulnerabilities and remediation suggestions.
challenges: The classifier can fall back to rules. Loading a base CodeBERT classifier does not demonstrate trained vulnerability accuracy, and generated patches require independent review.
architectureReference:
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        SolGuard AI Platform                     │
│                                                                 │
│  Phase 1        Phase 2        Phase 3        Phase 4           │
│  Lexical    →   Neural    →   Semantic   →   Patching   →  XAI │
│  Observer       Auditor       Architect      Agent        UI    │
│                                                                 │
│  AST/CFG        GNN/BERT      LLM CoT        OpenZeppelin       │
│  Slither        SmartBugs     GPT-4/Claude   Foundry/HH         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
problem: Contract vulnerabilities need more context than a single lint warning provides.
solution: Coordinate static findings, risk scoring, reasoning, and proposed patches as inspectable stages.
technicalDetails: The orchestrator loads agents independently and records which phases complete. Static analysis results feed risk classification and subsequent reasoning.
The classifier explicitly records codebert or rule_based as its model source. Optional dependency availability and model quality are separate from simply displaying a confidence score.

title: AutoLedger AI
subtitle: Adaptive blockchain research
description: A blockchain and reinforcement-learning exploration with a React dashboard and a simulated FastAPI network-state feed.
users: Developers exploring validator trust and adaptive network behavior.
features: Simulated node trust updates over WebSockets
architecture: simulated node state; separate PPO and ledger modules
challenges: The dashboard backend uses mock network state and random score changes. An integrated trained self-healing consensus network is not demonstrated by that feed.
problem: Validator behavior and trust changes are difficult to understand without a visible feedback loop.
solution: Explore trust scoring, consensus, and reinforcement-learning modules alongside a clearly simulated network dashboard.
technicalDetails: The FastAPI dashboard serves mock_network_state and changes node trust values on a WebSocket interval. It is a simulation rather than a production consensus feed.
A separate PyTorch actor-critic module samples actions and estimates values. Its presence does not establish that dashboard decisions are driven by a trained policy.

title: AI-Adaptive Linux Scheduler
subtitle: Workload scheduling visualization
description: A full-stack simulation of process metrics and rule-based priority adjustments, visualized through a responsive monitoring dashboard.
users: Learners exploring CPU pressure, process priorities, and scheduler trade-offs.
features: Priority adjustments above a load threshold
challenges: The backend does not modify a real Linux scheduler or run a trained model. Its AI optimization label refers to deterministic threshold logic over simulated processes.
architectureReference:
graph TD;
    A[React/Vite Frontend] -->|REST API Calls| B[Node.js Backend]
    B -->|Generates| C[Process Metrics]
    B -->|Evaluates Load| D[AI Optimizer Module]
    D -->|Throttles| C
    C -->|Sends JSON| A
problem: CPU pressure and priority adjustments are easier to study when process behavior is visible.
solution: Simulate process metrics and threshold-driven throttling through an Express API and charting interface.
technicalDetails: The Express service keeps process and metric history in memory and periodically generates workload fluctuations.
Above an aggregate CPU threshold, selected non-root simulated processes have CPU values reduced and nice values raised. This is rule-based simulation rather than a kernel scheduler integration.
